name: application-sidebar-search-filter
title: Sidebar Search Filter
description: Search input pinned above a nav list that live-filters items by label, highlighting the matched substring and showing a no-matches message when nothing matches.
useWhen: A sidebar or settings nav has enough items that scanning is slower than typing to find one.
You want immediate, client-side filtering as the user types, without a full page navigation or async request.
Highlighting the matched substring helps users confirm why an item matched.
avoidWhen: The nav has only a handful of items — a search box adds friction rather than saving time.
Matching needs to search more than the visible label (e.g. page content, tags) — wire in a real search index and result list instead of simple label filtering.
You need fuzzy or ranked search — this component does plain case-insensitive substring matching only.
responsiveBehavior: The filter input and list are a fixed w-56 column intended for a sidebar; both scale to their container's available width up to that cap.
accessibility: The input has a visually hidden label describing its purpose, since the placeholder alone isn't a reliable accessible name.
The no-matches message uses role="status" so it's announced as the result set changes to empty.
Matched text uses the semantic <mark> element rather than a styled <span>, so its significance is conveyed to assistive tech.

variants.title: Filtered results
variants.description: Search input with a query typed in, showing two matching nav items with the matched substring highlighted.
accessibility: Highlighted substrings use <mark>, which is announced distinctly by screen readers that support it.

variants.title: Filtered results (Dark)
variants.description: Filtered sidebar search state adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Highlight and text colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.

variants.title: No matches
variants.description: Empty-result state shown when the typed query matches no nav items.
accessibility: role="status" ensures the no-matches message is announced without requiring the user to look at the screen.

variants.title: No matches (Dark)
variants.description: No-matches state adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Message text color must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
